title: First hearing Bunk Johnson; not reaching New Orleans until 1919
summary: He first saw Bunk Johnson on an excursion, never heard Joe Oliver until Chicago, and only moved to New Orleans after the Army in 1919.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Did Buddy Bowling ever come out there?
You wouldn't know my band might go there.

No. I didn't never get to see him. I don't mean I wasn't old enough to see him, but I just never, I'll tell you the man I first seen when I was kind of getting on my feet with Trumpet, the first man I seen, I ain't gonna lie, it was Bunk Johnson. I seen him on my excursion pass our home recently, going to Homer, Louisiana, and I went on that excursion and I saw him play. First time. And I didn't ever see Joe Oliver until I went to Chicago.
That's a funny thing, you can live in the same town with people and never hear him.
Right. Well, I mean Dick, I didn't come to New Orleans until I left the Army. That was 1919. See what I mean?
I got discharged, instead of going back to Riesling, I come right on to New Orleans.
Well before the war, did you ever come into New Orleans at all?
Yeah, like we make a sugar grinder. I'll come in and buy clothes and things, but go right back.
No, never did, not in them time. No, I'll come in and get my clothes on Ramport Street and go right on back. Never did stay here to get no music.
How did Bunk play when you first heard him? Did he sound like his records is what I mean?
Yeah, he sounded just the same to me. He sounded just like them records.
How loud was he when you heard him in person?
Oh, he's pretty strong then. Yeah, he was strong, yeah.
Do you remember any of that?
Louder. Yeah, one piece I'll never forget he played, Alexander's Ragtime Band. He could play that all day for me.
Well, we'll play you the record of that sometime.
